subQuestions.questionText:

**My stumbling blocks became my stepping stones**
subQuestions.memoText:
- Responses could include circumstances/challenges that the narrator had overcome and that helped him/her to progress.

**Content and Planning (30 marks):**
- Exceptional (Upper 28–30 / Lower 25–27): Outstanding/striking response beyond normal expectations; intelligent, thought-provoking and mature ideas; exceptionally well organised and coherent, including introduction, body and conclusion.
- Skilful (Upper 22–24 / Lower 19–21): Very well-crafted response; fully relevant and interesting ideas with evidence of maturity; very well organised and coherent.
- Moderate (Upper 16–18 / Lower 13–15): Satisfactory response; ideas are reasonably coherent and convincing; reasonably organised and coherent.
- Elementary (Upper 10–12 / Lower 7–9): Inconsistently coherent response; unclear ideas and unoriginal; little evidence of organisation and coherence.
- Inadequate (Upper 4–6 / Lower 0–3): Totally irrelevant response; confused and unfocused ideas; vague and repetitive; unorganised and incoherent.

**Language, Style and Editing (15 marks):**
- Exceptional (Upper 14–15 / Lower 13): Tone, register, style and vocabulary highly appropriate; exceptionally impressive use of language; compelling and rhetorically effective; virtually error-free.

- Moderate (Upper 8–9 / Lower 7): Tone, register, style and vocabulary appropriate; appropriate use of language to convey meaning; rhetorical devices used to enhance content.
- Elementary (Upper 5–6 / Lower 4): Tone, register, style and vocabulary less appropriate; very basic use of language; tone and diction inappropriate; very limited vocabulary.
- Inadequate (0–3): Language incomprehensible; vocabulary limitations so extreme as to make comprehension impossible.

- 5: Excellent development of topic; exceptional detail; sentences and paragraphs exceptionally well-constructed.
- 4: Logical development of details; coherent; sentences and paragraphs logical, varied.
- 3: Relevant details developed; sentences and paragraphs well-constructed; essay still makes sense.
- 2: Some valid points; sentences and paragraphs faulty; essay still makes some sense.
- 0–1: Necessary points lacking; sentences and paragraphs faulty; essay lacks sense.

subQuestions.questionText:
**FORMAL SPEECH**

You are the spokesperson for the South African Olympics team, representing all sport codes.

Write your speech that will be televised prior to the team's departure.

*The body of your answer should be 180–200 words (20–25 lines) in length.*
subQuestions.memoText:
- The speech could be inspirational/motivational and/or galvanise public support/provide updates.
- Register should be appropriate.

**ASSESSMENT RUBRIC [25 MARKS]:**

**Content, Planning and Format (15 marks):**
- Exceptional (13–15): Outstanding response beyond normal expectations; intelligent and mature ideas; extensive knowledge of features of the type of text; writing maintains focus; coherence in content and ideas; highly elaborated and all details support the topic; appropriate and accurate format.
- Skilful (10–12): Very good response demonstrating good knowledge of features of the type of text; maintains focus – no digressions; coherent in content and ideas, very well elaborated and details support topic; appropriate format with minor inaccuracies.
- Moderate (7–9): Adequate response demonstrating knowledge of features of the type of text; not completely focused – some digressions; reasonably coherent in content and ideas; some details support the topic; generally appropriate format but with some inaccuracies.
- Elementary (4–6): Basic response demonstrating some knowledge of features of the type of text; some focus but writing digresses; not always coherent in content and ideas; few details support the topic; has vaguely applied necessary rules of format; some critical oversights.
- Inadequate (0–3): Response reveals no knowledge of features of the type of text; meaning is obscure with major digressions; not coherent in content and ideas; very few details support the topic; has not applied necessary rules of format.

**Language, Style and Editing (10 marks):**
- Exceptional (9–10): Tone, register, style and vocabulary highly appropriate to purpose, audience and context; grammatically accurate and well-constructed; virtually error-free.
- Skilful (7–8): Tone, register, style and vocabulary very appropriate; generally grammatically accurate and well-constructed; very good vocabulary; mostly free of errors.
- Moderate (5–6): Tone, register, style and vocabulary appropriate; some grammatical errors; adequate vocabulary; errors do not impede meaning.
- Elementary (3–4): Tone, register, style and vocabulary less appropriate; inaccurate grammar with numerous errors; limited vocabulary; meaning obscured.
- Inadequate (0–2): Tone, register, style and vocabulary do not correspond to purpose, audience and context; error-ridden and confused; vocabulary not suitable for purpose; meaning seriously impaired.

- Format: own address, date, addressee, subject line, salutation and signing-off.

**ASSESSMENT RUBRIC [25 MARKS]:**

**Content, Planning and Format (15 marks):**
- Exceptional (13–15): Outstanding response beyond normal expectations; intelligent and mature ideas; extensive knowledge of features of the type of text; writing maintains focus; coherence in content and ideas; highly elaborated and all details support the topic; appropriate and accurate format.
- Skilful (10–12): Very good response demonstrating good knowledge of features of the type of text; maintains focus – no digressions; coherent in content and ideas, very well elaborated and details support topic; appropriate format with minor inaccuracies.
- Moderate (7–9): Adequate response demonstrating knowledge of features of the type of text; not completely focused – some digressions; reasonably coherent in content and ideas; some details support the topic; generally appropriate format but with some inaccuracies.
- Elementary (4–6): Basic response demonstrating some knowledge of features of the type of text; some focus but writing digresses; not always coherent in content and ideas; few details support the topic; has vaguely applied necessary rules of format; some critical oversights.
- Inadequate (0–3): Response reveals no knowledge of features of the type of text; meaning is obscure with major digressions; not coherent in content and ideas; very few details support the topic; has not applied necessary rules of format.

**Language, Style and Editing (10 marks):**
- Exceptional (9–10): Tone, register, style and vocabulary highly appropriate to purpose, audience and context; grammatically accurate and well-constructed; virtually error-free.
- Skilful (7–8): Tone, register, style and vocabulary very appropriate; generally grammatically accurate and well-constructed; very good vocabulary; mostly free of errors.
- Moderate (5–6): Tone, register, style and vocabulary appropriate; some grammatical errors; adequate vocabulary; errors do not impede meaning.
- Elementary (3–4): Tone, register, style and vocabulary less appropriate; inaccurate grammar with numerous errors; limited vocabulary; meaning obscured.
- Inadequate (0–2): Tone, register, style and vocabulary do not correspond to purpose, audience and context; error-ridden and confused; vocabulary not suitable for purpose; meaning seriously impaired.

subQuestions.questionText:
**FORMAL REPORT**

The Youth Council, on which you serve, has raised a concern about the under-utilisation of libraries in the community. You have been tasked to investigate this matter.

Write the formal report that you will submit to the council.

*The body of your answer should be 180–200 words (20–25 lines) in length.*
